column1: To biomedical researchers all over the world, twins offer a precious opportunity to untangle the influence of genes and the environment — of nature and nurture.
column2: 对世界各地的生物医学研究者来说，双胞胎提供了一个宝贵机会，使他们能厘清基因与环境，也就是先天与后天各自的影响。

column1: Because identical twins come from a single fertilized egg that splits into two, they share virtually the same genetic code.
column2: 同卵双胞胎来自同一个分裂为二的受精卵，因此两人所拥有的遗传密码几乎完全相同。

column1: Any differences between them — one twin having younger looking skin, for example — must be due to environmental factors such as less time spent in the sun.
column2: 两人之间如有差异，比如其中一人的皮肤看起来更年轻，就应当归因于环境因素，例如晒太阳的时间较短。
column4: younger looking skin|看起来较年轻的皮肤

column1: Alternatively, by comparing the experiences of identical twins with those of fraternal twins, who come from separate eggs and share on average half their DNA, researchers can quantify the extent to which our genes affect our lives.
column2: 另一种方法，是把同卵双胞胎的经历同异卵双胞胎加以比较。异卵双胞胎来自不同的卵子，平均共享一半DNA。通过比较，研究者能量化基因对我们生活的影响程度。

column1: If identical twins are more similar to each other with respect to an ailment than fraternal twins are, then vulnerability to the disease must be rooted at least in part in heredity.
column2: 如果就某种病症而言，同卵双胞胎之间比异卵双胞胎之间更加相似，那么这种疾病的易感性至少有一部分必定源于遗传。
column7: at least in part|至少部分

column1: These two lines of research — studying the differences between identical twins to pinpoint the influence of environment, and comparing identical twins with fraternal ones to measure the role of inheritance — have been crucial to understanding the interplay of nature and nurture in determining our personalities, behavior, and vulnerability to disease.
column2: 这两条研究路径，一是通过同卵双胞胎之间的差异查明环境的影响，二是通过比较同卵与异卵双胞胎来衡量遗传的作用，对于理解先天与后天如何共同塑造个性、行为和对疾病的易感性至关重要。

column1: The idea of using twins to measure the influence of heredity dates back to 1875, when the English scientist Francis Galton first suggested the approach (and coined the phrase ‘nature and nurture’).
column2: 用双胞胎衡量遗传影响的想法可追溯至1875年。当时英国科学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿首次提出这种方法，还创造了“先天与后天”这一说法。
column7: coined the phrase|创造了这个说法

column1: But twin studies took a surprising twist in the 1980s, with the arrival of studies into identical twins who had been separated at birth and reunited as adults.
column2: 到了20世纪80年代，双胞胎研究出现了意想不到的转折：有人开始研究那些出生时就被分开、成年后才重聚的同卵双胞胎。
column3: took a surprising twist|出现意外转折
column4: with the arrival of|随着……出现
column6: separated at birth|出生时被分开

column1: Over two decades 137 sets of twins eventually visited Thomas Bouchard’s lab in what became known as the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart.
column2: 在二十年间，先后共有137对双胞胎来到托马斯·布沙尔的实验室，参与这项后来被称为“明尼苏达分开抚养双胞胎研究”的项目。
column4: sets of twins|一对对双胞胎

column1: Numerous tests were carried out on the twins, and they were each asked more than 15,000 questions.
column2: 研究者对双胞胎进行了大量测试，每个人都回答了超过15000个问题。

column1: Bouchard and his colleagues used this mountain of data to identify how far twins were affected by their genetic makeup.
column2: 布沙尔和同事们利用这海量数据，辨明双胞胎在多大程度上受到自身遗传构成的影响。

column1: The key to their approach was a statistical concept called heritability.
column2: 他们这一方法的关键，是一个叫作“遗传率”的统计学概念。

column1: In broad terms, the heritability of a trait measures the extent to which differences among members of a population can be explained by differences in their genetics.
column2: 大体而言，一项性状的遗传率衡量的是，在一个群体中，成员间该性状的差异有多大程度能用遗传差异来解释。
column6: members of a population|群体中的成员

column1: And wherever Bouchard and other scientists looked, it seemed, they found the invisible hand of genetic influence helping to shape our lives.
column2: 布沙尔等科学家无论将目光投向哪里，似乎都能发现遗传影响这只无形的手正在参与塑造我们的生活。
column6: shape our lives|塑造我们的生活

column1: Lately, however, twin studies have helped lead scientists to a radical new conclusion: that nature and nurture are not the only elemental forces at work.
column2: 不过，近年来双胞胎研究促使科学家得出了一个全新结论：先天和后天并不是仅有的两种基本影响力量。

column1: According to a recent field called epigenetics, there is a third factor also in play, one that in some cases serves as a bridge between the environment and our genes, and in others operates on its own to shape who we are.
column2: 新兴的表观遗传学认为，还有第三种因素在起作用。有时它在环境与基因之间充当桥梁，有时它又会独立发挥作用，塑造我们成为怎样的人。
column6: serves as a bridge|起桥梁作用
column7: operates on its own|独立起作用
column8: shape who we are|塑造我们成为怎样的人

column1: Epigenetic processes are chemical reactions tied to neither nature nor nurture but representing what researchers have called a ‘third component’.
column2: 表观遗传过程是一些化学反应，既不归于先天，也不归于后天，而代表了研究者所称的“第三种成分”。

column1: These reactions influence how our genetic code is expressed: how each gene is strengthened or weakened, even turned on or off, to build our bones, brains and all the other parts of our bodies.
column2: 这些反应影响遗传密码怎样表达：每个基因的作用会如何增强或减弱，甚至如何开启或关闭，由此形成骨骼、大脑及身体的其他部分。
column7: turned on or off|被开启或关闭

column1: If you think of our DNA as an immense piano keyboard and our genes as the keys — each key symbolizing a segment of DNA responsible for a particular note, or trait, and all the keys combining to make us who we are - then epigenetic processes determine when and how each key can be struck, changing the tune being played.
column2: 可以把DNA想象成一副巨大的钢琴键盘，把基因想象成琴键。每个琴键都象征一段DNA，负责一个特定的音符，也就是一种性状；所有琴键组合起来，造就了我们。表观遗传过程则决定每个琴键何时、怎样被按下，从而改变演奏出来的曲调。

column1: One way the study of epigenetics is revolutionizing our understanding of biology is by revealing a mechanism by which the environment directly impacts on genes.
column2: 表观遗传学之所以能革新我们对生物学的认识，其中一个原因是它揭示了一种机制，说明环境如何直接影响基因。

column1: Studies of animals, for example, have shown that when a rat experiences stress during pregnancy, it can cause epigenetic changes in a fetus that lead to behavioral problems as the rodent grows up.
column2: 例如，动物研究表明，雌鼠在妊娠期经历压力，可能引起胎鼠的表观遗传变化，以致幼鼠长大后出现行为问题。

column1: Other epigenetic processes appear to occur randomly, while others are normal, such as those that guide embryonic cells as they become heart, brain, or liver cells, for example.
column2: 另有一些表观遗传过程似乎是随机发生的，还有一些属于正常过程，例如引导胚胎细胞分化为心脏、脑或肝脏细胞的过程。

column1: Geneticist Danielle Reed has worked with many twins over the years and thought deeply about what twin studies have taught us.
column2: 遗传学家丹妮尔·里德多年来研究过许多双胞胎，并深入思考了双胞胎研究带给我们的认识。

column1: ‘It’s very clear when you look at twins that much of what they share is hardwired,’ she says.
column2: “观察双胞胎就很容易看出，两人共有的许多特征是与生俱来的。”她说。

column1: ‘Many things about them are absolutely the same and unalterable.
column2: “他们身上有许多特征完全相同，也无法改变。

column1: But it’s also clear, when you get to know them, that other things about them are different.
column2: 但熟悉他们之后，也能清楚地看到，他们在另一些方面并不一样。

column1: Epigenetics is the origin of a lot of those differences, in my view.’
column2: 在我看来，这许多差异正是源自表观遗传。”

column1: Reed credits Thomas Bouchard’s work for today’s surge in twin studies.
column2: 里德认为，今天双胞胎研究的蓬勃发展，应归功于托马斯·布沙尔的工作。

column1: ‘He was the trailblazer,’ she says.
column2: “他是开路先锋。”她说。

column1: ‘We forget that 50 years ago things like heart disease were thought to be caused entirely by lifestyle.
column2: “我们往往忘了，50年前人们还认为心脏病之类的疾病完全是由生活方式造成的。
column4: were thought to be|当时被认为

column1: Schizophrenia was thought to be due to poor mothering.
column2: 当时人们还认为精神分裂症源于母亲养育不当。
column4: was thought to be|当时被认为是

column1: Twin studies have allowed us to be more reflective about what people are actually born with and what’s caused by experience.’
column2: 双胞胎研究让我们能更审慎地思考，哪些特征确实是人与生俱来的，哪些则由后天经历造成。”
column6: caused by experience|由后天经历造成

column1: Having said that, Reed adds, the latest work in epigenetics promises to take our understanding even further.
column2: 不过，里德补充说，表观遗传学的最新研究有望让我们的认识更进一步。

column1: ‘What I like to say is that nature writes some things in pencil and some things in pen,’ she says.
column2: “我喜欢这样说，大自然有些东西用铅笔写，有些用钢笔写。”她说。

column1: ‘Things written in pen you can’t change.
column2: “用钢笔写下的东西，你改不了。
column3: written in pen|用钢笔写下的

column1: That’s DNA.
column2: 那就是DNA。

column1: But things written in pencil you can.
column2: 但用铅笔写下的东西，你可以改。
column3: written in pencil|用铅笔写下的

column1: That’s epigenetics.
column2: 那就是表观遗传。

column1: Now that we’re actually able to look at the DNA and see where the pencil writings are, it’s sort of a whole new world.’
column2: 如今，我们真的能查看DNA，找出铅笔的字迹留在哪里，仿佛一下子走进了一个全新的世界。”
column7: a whole new world|一个全新的世界
